title: Negation
focus: na with present/future, ni for past (ami khaini), nei for 'there isn't / don't have', na for 'not' with adjectives.
body:
# Negation

Bengali has three little words for "not", and each tense picks one.

**na** goes **after** the verb in the present, the future and the continuous: **ami cha khai na** (I don't drink tea), **ami jabo na** (I won't go), **ami khacchi na** (I'm not eating).

**-ni** is for the past. Don't use the past forms (khelam, kheyechi) at all. Take the **present** form and stick **-ni** on the end: **ami khai** → **ami khaini** (I didn't eat / I haven't eaten). One form covers both "didn't" and "haven't".

**nei** means "there isn't" or "don't have". It's the opposite of **ache** (there is / is at): **jol nei** (there's no water), **amar boi nei** (I don't have a book), **Ollie barite nei** (Ollie isn't home).

**na** also negates adjectives and descriptions: **eta bhalo na** (this isn't good), **cha-ta gorom na** (the tea isn't hot).

| | Positive | Negative |
|---|---|---|
| present | ami khai | ami khai **na** |
| future | ami jabo | ami jabo **na** |
| continuous | ami khacchi | ami khacchi **na** |
| past | ami khelam / kheyechi | ami **khaini** |
| tumi past | tumi khele | tumi **khaoni** |
| o past | o khelo | o **khayni** |
| have / there is | amar boi ache | amar boi **nei** |
| adjective | eta bhalo | eta bhalo **na** |

## Examples

- **ami aaj jabo na**: I won't go today
- **ami khaini**: I didn't eat / I haven't eaten
- **tumi khaoni?**: haven't you eaten?
- **Ollie khayni**: Ollie hasn't eaten
- **o asheni**: he/she hasn't come
- **ami tomake bolini**: I didn't tell you
- **tomake jete hobe na**: you don't have to go
- **jol nei**: there's no water
- **ekhane keu nei**: there's nobody here
- **Ollie dushtu na, o lokkhi beral**: Ollie isn't naughty, he's a good cat

## Common mistakes

- ❌ **ami khelam na**. The past never takes na. Use the present form + ni: ✅ **ami khaini**.
- ❌ **amar boi na**. For "don't have" and "isn't there", use ✅ **amar boi nei**.
